acceptance: A unit test over a grid of estimate and available values shows that in every refusal message the available figure printed is below the threshold figure printed, at the precision printed.
The refusal message states the estimate, the margin and the resulting threshold, and says the estimate is for the full benchmark at that scale factor.
A test shows the admit/refuse decision is unchanged for inputs on both sides of the threshold, including the three cases above (3.0 vs 3.5, 2.0 vs 2.4, 3.0 vs 3.1 GB).
`make batch-member-check TESTS=tests/unit/core/dataframe/test_dataframe_capabilities.py` passes; `make comment-policy-check` reports nothing for the touched files.
A `changelog.d/` fragment describes the clearer message.

description:
Problem. `check_sufficient_memory` in `benchbox/core/dataframe/capabilities.py` refuses a run when available memory is below the estimate plus a 20% safety margin (`required_with_margin`), but its message prints the bare estimate. On 2026-11-12 users saw `Insufficient memory: ~3.0 GB required, but only 3.5 GB available`, `~2.0 GB required, but only 2.4 GB available` and `~3.0 GB required, but only 3.1 GB available`: the available figure exceeds the figure called required, so the message does not say how much memory to free. The estimate is also for the whole benchmark at that scale factor even when `--queries` selects a few queries, and the message does not say so (a three-query TPC-DS SF10 run is refused with `~18-20 GB required`).

Owner decision 2026-11-13: fix the message only. The refusal must show the threshold actually compared (estimate plus margin), name the margin, and say the estimate covers the full benchmark at that scale regardless of a query subset. The passing message must be consistent with it. Do not change the estimate, the margin, or what is refused. Estimating from the tables a query subset reads is out of scope here and tracked in df-memory-guard-subset-estimate-20261113.

Frozen scope: `benchbox/core/dataframe/capabilities.py`, `tests/unit/core/dataframe/test_dataframe_capabilities.py`.

Guardrails (members of batch df-platform-followups):
- Stay inside the frozen scope below; a path outside it is refused at landing. If the work needs another path, stop and report it.
- No explanatory comments or docstrings (COMMENT-POLICY-001). Search for an existing helper before adding one (`make duplicate-check-delta`).
- Do not edit SQL text, reference answers, expected-result fixtures or baselines to make a check pass.
- Members make no tracker write, open no PR, do not run the fast tier, benchmarks or timing runs, and never force heavy-work admission. They use absolute paths under their own worktree and stop at a landing report.
- One `changelog.d/` fragment per member.
- The numeric decision (`available >= required_with_margin`) must not change; a test pins that the same inputs are refused or admitted as before.
- Keep `MemoryCheckResult` fields and their meaning; other code and JSON output read them.
